the-intellectual-development-of-the-cana: Sir John Bourinot, clerk of Canada's Parliament, follows the rise of his country's books, schools, and learned clubs. From French roots through Confederation he maps a young people's growing mind. A landmark work, and still the best first guide to Canada's inner life.
the-humorous-poetry-of-the-english-langu: James Parton anthologizes five centuries of English comic verse, from Chaucer's sly tales to the newspaper humorists of his own day. Hood, Holmes, Saxe, and dozens more contribute laughs in rhyme. A big, merry book for anyone who believes poetry should sometimes simply make you grin.
memoirs-of-general-lafayette-with-an-acc: Samuel Knapp's memoirs of General Lafayette — with the full story of his triumphal 1824 visit to America — honor the French hero of two revolutions. His warm account preserves a young nation's gratitude. A patriotic American tribute, full of feeling. Bunker Hill's old soldier wept to see the cheering crowds.
the-history-of-roman-literature-from-the: Charles Cruttwell's History of Roman Literature runs from the earliest period to the death of Marcus Aurelius — a full survey of Latin letters. His scholarly care and clear judgment served students for decades. A thorough and trustworthy guide to Rome's writers.
